The '''Fulkerson Prize''' for outstanding papers in the area of [[discrete mathematics]] is sponsored jointly by the [[Mathematical Optimization Society]] (MOS)  and the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS). Up to three awards of $1,500 each are presented at each (triennial) International Symposium of the MOS. Originally, the prizes were paid out of a memorial fund administered by the AMS that was established by friends of the late [[Delbert Ray Fulkerson]] to encourage mathematical excellence in the fields of research exemplified by his work. The prizes are now funded by an endowment administered by MOS.

==Winners==
* 1979: 
** [[Richard M. Karp]] for classifying many important [[NP-complete]] problems.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Karp | first1 = Richard M. | author-link = Richard M. Karp | year = 1975 | title = On the computational complexity of combinatorial problems | journal = Networks | volume = 5 | pages = 45–68 | doi=10.1002/net.1975.5.1.45}}</ref>
** [[Kenneth Appel]] and [[Wolfgang Haken]] for the [[four color theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Appel | first1 = Kenneth | author-link = Kenneth Appel | author-link2 = Wolfgang Haken | last2 = Haken | first2 = Wolfgang | year = 1977 | title = Every planar map is four colorable, Part I: Discharging | journal = [[Illinois Journal of Mathematics]] | volume = 21 | pages = 429–490 }}</ref>
** [[Paul Seymour (mathematician)|Paul Seymour]] for generalizing the [[max-flow min-cut theorem]] to [[matroid]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Seymour | first1 = Paul | author-link = Paul Seymour (mathematician) | year = 1977 | title = The matroids with the max-flow min-cut property | journal = [[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]] | volume = 23 | issue = 2–3 | pages = 189–222 | doi=10.1016/0095-8956(77)90031-4| doi-access = free }}</ref>
* 1982: 
** D.B. Judin, [[Arkadi Nemirovski]], [[Leonid Khachiyan]], [[Martin Grötschel]], [[László Lovász]] and [[Alexander Schrijver]] for the [[ellipsoid method]] in [[linear programming]] and [[combinatorial optimization]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Judin | first1 = D.B. | author-link2 = Arkadi Nemirovski | last2 = Nemirovski | first2 = Arkadi | year = 1976 | title = Informational complexity and effective methods of solution for convex extremal problems | journal = Ekonomika I Matematicheskie Metody | volume = 12 | pages = 357–369 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Khachiyan | first1 = Leonid | author-link = Leonid Khachiyan | year = 1979 | title = A polynomial algorithm in linear programming | journal = Akademiia Nauk SSSR. Doklady | volume = 244 | pages = 1093–1096 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|newspaper=[[Boston Globe]]|url=https://archive.boston.com/news/globe/obituaries/articles/2005/05/05/leonid_khachiyan_professor_leading_computer_scientist/|date=May 5, 2005|title=Leonid Khachiyan, professor, leading computer scientist}}.</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Grötschel | first1 = Martin | author-link2 = László Lovász | author-link3 = Alexander Schrijver | last2 = Lovász | first2 = László | last3 = Schrijver | first3 = Alexander | year = 1981 | title = The ellipsoid method and its consequences in combinatorial optimization | journal = [[Combinatorica]] | volume = 1 | issue = 2 | pages = 169–197 | doi=10.1007/bf02579273}}</ref>
**[[Georgy Petrovich Egorychev|G. P. Egorychev]] and D. I. Falikman for proving [[Van der Waerden's conjecture]] that the matrix with all entries equal has the smallest [[Permanent (mathematics)|permanent]] of any [[doubly stochastic matrix]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Egorychev | first1 = G. P. | year = 1981 | title = The solution of van der Waerden's problem for permanents | journal = Akademiia Nauk SSSR. Doklady | volume = 258 | pages = 1041–1044 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Falikman | first1 = D. I. | year = 1981 | title = A proof of the van der Waerden conjecture on the permanent of a doubly stochastic matrix | journal = Matematicheskie Zametki | volume = 29 | pages = 931–938 }}</ref>
** 
* 1985: 
** [[Jozsef Beck]] for tight bounds on the [[discrepancy theory|discrepancy]] of [[arithmetic progression]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Beck | first1 = Jozsef | author-link = Jozsef Beck | year = 1981 | title = Roth's estimate of the discrepancy of integer sequences is nearly sharp | journal = [[Combinatorica]] | volume = 1 | issue = 4| pages = 319–325 | doi=10.1007/bf02579452}}</ref>
** [[Hendrik Lenstra|H. W. Lenstra Jr.]] for using the [[geometry of numbers]] to solve [[integer program]]s with few variables in time polynomial in the number of constraints.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Lenstra | first1 = H. W. Jr. | author-link = Hendrik Lenstra | year = 1983 | title = Integer programming with a fixed number of variables | journal = Mathematics of Operations Research | volume = 8 | issue = 4| pages = 538–548 | doi=10.1287/moor.8.4.538}}</ref>
** [[Eugene M. Luks]] for a [[polynomial time]] [[graph isomorphism problem|graph isomorphism algorithm]] for graphs of bounded [[degree (graph theory)|maximum degree]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Luks | first1 = Eugene M. | year = 1982 | title = Isomorphism of graphs of bounded valence can be tested in polynomial time | journal = Journal of Computer and System Sciences | volume = 25 | issue = 1| pages = 42–65 | doi=10.1016/0022-0000(82)90009-5| doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=w_hVAAAAIBAJ&sjid=huEDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6539,2351404&dq=fulkerson-prize&hl=en|newspaper=[[The Register-Guard|Eugene Register-Guard]]|title=U of O Computer Chief Gets Top Award|date=August 10, 1985}}.</ref>
* 1988: 
** [[Éva Tardos]] for finding [[circulation problem|minimum cost circulations]] in [[Time complexity|strongly polynomial time]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Tardos | first1 = Éva | author-link = Éva Tardos | year = 1985 | title = A strongly polynomial minimum cost circulation algorithm | journal = [[Combinatorica]] | volume = 5 | issue = 3 | pages = 247–256 | doi=10.1007/bf02579369}}</ref>
** [[Narendra Karmarkar]] for [[Karmarkar's algorithm]] for [[linear programming]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Karmarkar | first1 = Narendra | author-link = Narendra Karmarkar | year = 1984 | title = A new polynomial-time algorithm for linear programming | journal = [[Combinatorica]] | volume = 4 | issue = 4 | pages = 373–395 | doi=10.1007/bf02579150}}</ref>
* 1991: 
** [[Martin Dyer|Martin E. Dyer]], [[Alan M. Frieze]] and [[Ravindran Kannan]] for [[random walk|random-walk]]-based [[approximation algorithm]]s for the volume of convex bodies.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Dyer | first1 = Martin E. | author-link = Martin Dyer | author-link2 = Alan M. Frieze | author-link3 = Ravindran Kannan | last2 = Frieze | first2 = Alan M. | last3 = Kannan | first3 = Ravindran | year = 1991 | title = A random polynomial time algorithm for approximating the volume of convex bodies | journal = [[Journal of the ACM]] | volume = 38 | issue = 1| pages = 1–17 | doi=10.1145/102782.102783}}</ref>
** Alfred Lehman for [[Logical matrix|0,1-matrix]] analogues of the theory of [[perfect graph]]s.<ref>Alfred Lehman, "The width-length inequality and degenerate projective planes," W. Cook and P. D. Seymour (eds.), Polyhedral Combinatorics, DIMACS Series in Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science, volume 1, (American Mathematical Society, 1990) pp. 101-105.</ref>
** Nikolai E. Mnev for [[Mnev's universality theorem]], that every semialgebraic set is equivalent to the space of realizations of an [[oriented matroid]].<ref>Nikolai E. Mnev, "The universality theorems on the classification problem of configuration varieties and convex polytope varieties," O. Ya. Viro (ed.), Topology and Geometry-Rohlin Seminar, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1346 (Springer-Verlag, Berlin, 1988) pp. 527-544.</ref>
* 1994: 
** [[Louis Billera]] for finding bases of piecewise-polynomial function spaces over triangulations of space.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Billera | first1 = Louis | year = 1988 | title = Homology of smooth splines: Generic triangulations and a conjecture of Strang | journal = [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume = 310 | issue = 1 | pages = 325–340 | doi=10.2307/2001125| doi-access = free | jstor = 2001125 }}</ref>
** [[Gil Kalai]] for making progress on the [[Hirsch conjecture]] by proving subexponential bounds on the diameter of ''d''-dimensional polytopes with ''n'' facets.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Kalai | first1 = Gil | author-link = Gil Kalai | year = 1992 | title = Upper bounds for the diameter and height of graphs of the convex polyhedra | journal = [[Discrete and Computational Geometry]] | volume = 8 | issue = 4 | pages = 363–372 | doi=10.1007/bf02293053| doi-access = free }}</ref>
** [[Neil Robertson (mathematician)|Neil Robertson]], [[Paul Seymour (mathematician)|Paul Seymour]] and [[Robin Thomas (mathematician)|Robin Thomas]] for the six-color case of [[Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)|Hadwiger's conjecture]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Robertson | first1 = Neil | author-link = Neil Robertson (mathematician) | author-link2 = Paul Seymour (mathematician) | author-link3 = Robin Thomas (mathematician) | last2 = Seymour | first2 = Paul | last3 = Thomas | first3 = Robin | year = 1993 | title = Hadwiger's conjecture for K_6-free graphs | journal = [[Combinatorica]] | volume = 13 | issue = 3 | pages = 279–361 | doi=10.1007/bf01202354}}</ref>
* 1997: 
**[[Jeong Han Kim]] for finding the [[asymptotic analysis|asymptotic growth rate]] of the [[Ramsey number]]s ''R''(3,''t'').<ref>{{cite journal | last = Kim | first = Jeong Han | author-link = Jeong Han Kim | doi = 10.1002/rsa.3240070302 | issue = 3 | journal = Random Structures & Algorithms | mr = 1369063 | pages = 173–207 | title = The Ramsey number ''R''(3,''t'') has order of magnitude ''t''<sup>2</sup>/log&nbsp;''t'' | volume = 7 | year = 1995}}.</ref>
* 2000: 
** [[Michel Goemans|Michel X. Goemans]] and [[David P. Williamson]] for [[approximation algorithm]]s based on [[semidefinite programming]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Goemans | first1 = Michel X. | last2 = Williamson | first2 = David P. | year = 1995 | title = Improved approximation algorithms for the maximum cut and satisfiability probelsm using semi-definite programming | journal = [[Journal of the ACM]] | volume = 42 | issue = 6| pages = 1115–1145 | doi=10.1145/227683.227684| doi-access = free }}</ref>
** Michele Conforti, [[Gérard Cornuéjols]], and [[Mendu Rammohan Rao|M. R. Rao]] for recognizing [[Balanced matrix|balanced 0-1 matrices]] in [[polynomial time]].<ref>Michele Conforti, Gérard Cornuéjols, and [[Mendu Rammohan Rao|M. R. Rao]], "Decomposition of balanced matrices", ''[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]]'', Series B, 77 (2): 292–406, 1999.</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=MR Rao New Dean Of ISB|newspaper=[[The Financial Express (India)|Financial Express]]|date=July 2, 2004|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/mr-rao-new-dean-of-isb/109506/}}.</ref>
* 2003:
** [[Jim Geelen|J. F. Geelen]], A. M. H. Gerards and A. Kapoor for the [[finite field|GF(4)]] case of [[Rota's conjecture]] on [[matroid minor]]s.<ref>[[Jim Geelen|J. F. Geelen]], A. M. H. Gerards and A. ** Bertrand Guenin for a [[forbidden graph characterization|forbidden minor characterization]] of the weakly bipartite graphs (graphs whose bipartite subgraph polytope is 0-1).<ref>Bertrand Guenin, "A characterization of weakly bipartite graphs," ''[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]]'', Series B, 83 (1): 112–168, 2001.</ref><ref name="fpc03"/>
** Satoru Iwata, Lisa Fleischer, Satoru Fujishige, and [[Alexander Schrijver]] for showing [[Submodular set function#Optimization problems|submodular minimization]] to be strongly polynomial.<ref>Satoru Iwata, Lisa Fleischer, Satoru Fujishige, "A combinatorial strongly polynomial algorithm for minimizing submodular functions," ''[[Journal of the ACM]]'', 48 (4): 761–777, 2001.</ref><ref>[[Alexander Schrijver]], "A combinatorial algorithm minimizing submodular functions in strongly polynomial time," ''[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]]'', Series B 80 (2): 346–355, 2000.</ref><ref name="fpc03"/>
* 2006:
** [[Manindra Agrawal]], [[Neeraj Kayal]] and [[Nitin Saxena]], for the [[AKS primality test]].<ref>[[Manindra Agrawal]], [[Neeraj Kayal]] and [[Nitin Saxena]], "PRIMES is in P," ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'', 160 (2): 781–793, 2004.</ref><ref>{{cite news|newspaper=[[The Hindu]]|date=June 11, 2009|first=M. ** [[Neil Robertson (mathematician)|Neil Robertson]] and [[Paul Seymour (mathematician)|Paul Seymour]], for the [[Robertson–Seymour theorem]] showing that [[graph minor]]s form a [[well-quasi-ordering]].<ref>[[Neil Robertson (mathematician)|Neil Robertson]] and [[Paul Seymour (mathematician)|Paul Seymour]],  "Graph Minors. * 2009:
** [[Maria Chudnovsky]], Neil Robertson, Paul Seymour, and Robin Thomas, for the [[strong perfect graph theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Chudnovsky | first1 = Maria | author-link = Maria Chudnovsky | last2 = Robertson | first2 = Neil | last3 = Seymour | first3 = Paul | last4 = Thomas | first4 = Robin | year = 2006 | title = The strong perfect graph theorem | journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]] | volume = 164 | pages = 51–229 | doi=10.4007/annals.2006.164.51| arxiv = math/0212070 }}</ref><ref name="fpc09">[http://www.mathopt.org/?nav=fulkerson_2009 2009 Fulkerson Prize citation], retrieved 2012-08-19.</ref>
** [[Daniel A. Spielman]] and [[Shang-Hua Teng]], for [[smoothed analysis]] of [[linear programming]] algorithms.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Spielman | first1 = Daniel A. | author-link = Daniel A. Spielman | author-link2 = Shang-Hua Teng | last2 = Teng | first2 = Shang-Hua | year = 2004 | title = Smoothed analysis of algorithms: Why the simplex algorithm usually takes polynomial time | journal = [[Journal of the ACM]] | volume = 51 | pages = 385–463 | doi=10.1145/990308.990310| arxiv = math/0212413 }}</ref><ref name="fpc09"/>
** [[Thomas Callister Hales|Thomas C. Hales]] and Samuel P. Ferguson, for proving the [[Kepler conjecture]] on the densest possible [[sphere packing]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Hales | first1 = Thomas C. | author-link = Thomas Callister Hales | year = 2005 | title = A proof of the Kepler conjecture | doi = 10.4007/annals.2005.162.1065 | journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]] | volume = 162 | issue = 3 | pages = 1063–1183 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Ferguson | first1 = Samuel P. | year = 2006 | title = Sphere Packings, V. Pentahedral Prisms | journal = [[Discrete and Computational Geometry]] | volume = 36 | pages = 167–204 | doi=10.1007/s00454-005-1214-y| doi-access = free }}</ref><ref name="fpc09"/>

** [[Sanjeev Arora (computer scientist)|Sanjeev Arora]], [[Satish Rao]], and [[Umesh Vazirani]] for improving the [[approximation ratio]] for [[Vertex separator|graph separators]] and related problems from <math>O(\log n)</math> to <math>O(\sqrt{\log n})</math>.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Arora | first1 = Sanjeev | author-link = Sanjeev Arora (computer scientist) | author-link3 = Umesh Vazirani | last2 = Rao | first2 = Satish | last3 = Vazirani | first3 = Umesh | year = 2009 | title = Expander flows, geometric embeddings and graph partitioning | journal = [[Journal of the ACM]] | volume = 56 | issue = 2 | pages = 1–37 | doi=10.1145/1502793.1502794}}</ref>

** [[László Lovász]] and [[Balázs Szegedy]] for characterizing subgraph multiplicity in sequences of [[dense graph]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Lovász | first1 = László | author-link = László Lovász | last2 = Szegedy | first2 = Balázs | year = 2006 | title = Limits of dense graph sequences | journal = [[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]] | volume = 96 | issue = 6 | pages = 933–957 | doi=10.1016/j.jctb.2006.05.002| arxiv = math/0408173 }}</ref>
